paragraphs.title: God’s Goodness and the Crisis Caused by the Wicked’s Success

answers: To Israel and those with a clean heart
easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart.”
easy.q: To whom is God good according to the opening verse?

easy.explanation: He says, “my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped.”
easy.q: What nearly happened to the poet?

easy.explanation: He says, “I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.”
easy.q: At whom was the poet envious?

answers: He saw the peace and strength of the wicked
medium.explanation: He saw that the wicked had firm strength and were not troubled like other men.
medium.q: Why did the poet experience a crisis?

answers: He nearly turned from the right way
medium.explanation: The words describe a near spiritual stumbling or turning away.
medium.q: What does “my feet were almost gone” mean in context?

answers: God is good, yet the wicked’s prosperity causes doubt
The wicked suffer while the righteous prosper
The poet becomes rich while Israel is poor
medium.explanation: The opening declares God’s goodness, while the wicked’s apparent success creates a struggle.
medium.q: What contrast appears in these verses?

answers: Lack of knowledge about God’s name
The gap between his faith and the condition of the wicked
challenge.explanation: He struggled with seeing wicked people prosper while he sought righteousness.
challenge.q: What caused the poet nearly to stray despite declaring that God is good?

answers: The poet describes the inner struggle of someone trying to remain upright
The poet claims that all wicked people are pure
The poet withdraws his belief in God’s goodness
challenge.explanation: The verse places purity of heart beside the temptation created by the wicked’s prosperity.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the connection between “a clean heart” and the poet’s envy?

answers: Strength and freedom from visible suffering
challenge.explanation: They have firm strength and are not troubled or plagued like other men.
challenge.q: Which condition of the wicked is emphasized most in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Wicked’s Arrogance and Their Challenge to Divine Order

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Therefore pride compasseth them about as a chain.”
easy.q: What surrounds the wicked like a chain?

easy.explanation: They speak wickedly concerning oppression and speak loftily.

answers: Whether He is good to Israel
How God knows and whether there is knowledge in the most High
Whether He is present on earth
easy.explanation: They ask, “How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the most High?”
easy.q: What do they ask about God?

answers: Abundance causes them to abandon their strength
medium.explanation: Their prosperity is associated with pride, violence, and arrogant speech.
medium.q: What is the relationship between abundance and the wicked’s behavior?

medium.explanation: The word refers to violent or oppressive treatment of others.
medium.q: What does “violence” mean in this passage?

answers: Their mouth is against heaven and their tongue walks through the earth
Their words remain only in their hearts
They do not speak at all
medium.explanation: Their speech is portrayed as bold, widespread, and directed against heaven.
medium.q: How is the influence of their speech described?

answers: They trust completely in God’s supervision
They doubt God’s knowledge and supervision
challenge.explanation: Their question expresses doubt that God knows or observes their actions.
challenge.q: What does the question “How doth God know?” reveal about the wicked?

challenge.explanation: Their abundance leads to pride and violence, followed by speech challenging divine order.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes the wicked’s decline?

answers: The wicked act unjustly yet gain power and prosperity
God is not mentioned at all
challenge.explanation: Although they are violent and arrogant, the wicked prosper and increase in riches.
challenge.q: What is the central paradox in this passage?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Person’s Doubts and Turning to the Sanctuary

easy.explanation: He says, “Verily I have cleansed my heart in vain.”
easy.q: How does the poet feel about cleansing his heart?

easy.explanation: He says, “For all the day long have I been plagued.”
easy.q: What happened to the poet throughout the day?

answers: To the place of the wicked
easy.explanation: He says, “Until I went into the sanctuary of God.”
easy.q: Where did the poet go to understand these things?

answers: He feared offending the generation of God’s children
He did not want to speak to God
medium.explanation: He says that speaking in this way would offend the generation of God’s children.
medium.q: Why was the poet afraid to speak openly about his thoughts?

medium.explanation: The poet describes himself as suffering throughout the day.
medium.q: What does “plagued” mean in this context?

answers: Doubt leads him to seek understanding in God’s sanctuary
Doubt causes him to abandon God
Doubt is solved by gaining wealth
medium.explanation: Because he cannot understand the situation, he goes to the sanctuary and gains insight.
medium.q: What is the connection between doubt and going to the sanctuary?

answers: Trying to understand the situation was a heavy burden
challenge.explanation: The poet describes his effort to understand as painful and difficult.
challenge.q: What does “it was too painful for me” express?

answers: He does not want to harm the faith of the generation
The wicked forbid him to speak
challenge.explanation: He fears that speaking would offend God’s children.
challenge.q: Why does the poet not immediately announce his doubts?

answers: Understanding the end of the wicked
challenge.explanation: In the sanctuary he understands the destiny or end of the wicked.
challenge.q: What is revealed as the purpose of entering the sanctuary?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Surely thou didst set them in slippery places.”
easy.q: Where did God place the wicked?

answers: They are brought down into destruction
easy.explanation: The verses describe their being cast down into destruction and desolation.
easy.q: What happens to the wicked in the end?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “As a dream when one awaketh.”
easy.q: What is their disappearance compared to?

answers: It is temporary and may end suddenly
It does not exist at all
medium.explanation: They are brought into desolation “in a moment.”
medium.q: What is shown about the wicked’s prosperity?

medium.explanation: The word describes their ruin and destruction.
medium.q: What does “destruction” mean in this passage?

answers: Their apparently pleasant position leads to a fall
The slippery place protects them forever
The slippery place is their home
medium.explanation: Their seemingly secure position is unstable and ends in downfall.
medium.q: What is the connection between slippery places and the wicked’s end?

answers: It passes away and disappears as if it never existed
It is given only to the righteous
challenge.explanation: Like a dream after waking, their apparent success quickly vanishes.
challenge.q: What does the image of a dream teach about the wicked’s prosperity?

answers: He sees outward success as the final reality
He understands that outward success does not reveal the end
He decides to imitate the wicked
challenge.explanation: In the sanctuary he learns that temporary appearances do not determine the final outcome.
challenge.q: What change in perspective occurs in the poet?

answers: It happens only after a very long time
It has no connection with time
challenge.explanation: The phrase stresses the suddenness of their destruction.
challenge.q: What does “in a moment” emphasize about the wicked’s downfall?

easy.explanation: He says his heart was grieved and admits that he was foolish and ignorant.
He says, “thou hast holden me by my right hand.”
easy.q: By what does God hold the poet?

answers: He hides him from the world
He gives him the wicked’s riches
easy.explanation: The poet says, “Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel.”
easy.q: What does God do for the poet?

answers: As one who always knew everything
medium.explanation: He says, “So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.”
medium.q: How does the poet describe himself after gaining understanding?

answers: The inner and emotional part of a person
medium.explanation: In this context, the reins represent the inward thoughts and feelings.
medium.q: What does “my reins” refer to in “I was pricked in my reins”?

answers: His confession leads him to recognize that God holds and guides him
His confession causes him to reject God
medium.explanation: After admitting his ignorance, he emphasizes God’s continuing presence and guidance.
medium.q: What is the connection between the poet’s confession of ignorance and God’s help?

answers: The poet is limited and does not understand, but God guides him
The poet knows everything and God is silent
challenge.explanation: The poet admits his limitations while describing God’s faithful guidance.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in verses 21–24?

answers: The poet experiences God’s continuing presence after the crisis
The poet wants to leave God
challenge.explanation: The words emphasize the continuing relationship between God and the poet.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “I am continually with thee”?

answers: To the wealth of the wicked
challenge.explanation: The poet says, “afterward receive me to glory.”
challenge.q: Where does God’s guidance lead the poet afterward?

paragraphs.title: Closeness to God as the Greatest Good

easy.explanation: He says, “Whom have I in heaven but thee?”
easy.q: Who is first in the poet’s desires?

easy.explanation: He says, “God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.”
He says, “it is good for me to draw near to God.”
easy.q: What is good for the poet according to the conclusion?

answers: They will be received to glory
They will become the poet’s portion
medium.explanation: The psalm says, “they that are far from thee shall perish.”
medium.q: What will happen to those who are far from God?

answers: A place of confidence and refuge
medium.explanation: Trusting in the Lord means relying on Him for security and help.
medium.q: What does “my trust” represent in “I have put my trust in the Lord GOD”?

medium.explanation: He says that he will declare all God’s works.
medium.q: What will the poet do after putting his trust in God?

answers: Material prosperity is the highest good
Closeness to God and trust in Him matter more than outward success
There is no difference between the righteous and the wicked
challenge.explanation: The poet identifies God as his portion, strength, and refuge rather than wealth or status.
challenge.q: What value-based conclusion follows from the final verses?

answers: God is his inner foundation and strength
God is only an external possession
God causes him to withdraw from others
challenge.explanation: The poet describes God as the strength of his heart and his portion forever.
challenge.q: How does “the strength of my heart” relate to the poet’s conclusion?

answers: The poet decides that the wicked are right
The poet recognizes that closeness to God is the true good
The poet stops believing in God’s goodness
challenge.explanation: He ends by valuing nearness to God and declaring His works above the success of the wicked.
challenge.q: How does the process that began with envy of the wicked end?
